RUNX1 CHROMATIN OCCUPANCY CHANGES UPON CBFβ-SMMHC INHIBITION
============================================================

SUMMARY
-------
Pharmacological inhibition of CBFβ-SMMHC by AI-10-49 in human inv(16) AML cells (ME-1) causes a massive, genome-wide gain of RUNX1 chromatin occupancy. RUNX1 peak count increases 6.9-fold (1,329 → 9,169 peaks), with genomic coverage expanding 9.7-fold (0.33 → 3.18 Mb). Nearly all existing DMSO binding sites are retained (92.7%), while 7,950 new binding sites are gained. This demonstrates that CBFβ-SMMHC sequestration — not chromatin accessibility — is the primary barrier to RUNX1 engagement with its genomic targets.

KEY QUANTITATIVE FINDINGS
--------------------------
1. RUNX1 peak expansion: 1,329 (DMSO) → 9,169 (AI-10-49), a 6.9-fold increase
2. Genomic coverage: 0.33 Mb (DMSO) → 3.18 Mb (AI-10-49), a 9.7-fold increase
3. Peak retention: 92.7% of DMSO peaks (1,232/1,329) are maintained after treatment
4. New binding sites: 7,950 peaks gained in AI-10-49 (86.7% of the AI-10-49 peak set)
5. Peaks lost: Only 97 (7.3% of DMSO peaks), confirming this is a gain-of-binding event, not redistribution
6. Jaccard index: 0.0935 (low due to expansion); Overlap coefficient: 0.9270 (high retention)
7. H3K27ac remains stable: 57,828 (DMSO) vs 56,299 (AI-10-49) peaks, Jaccard 0.66

GAINED PEAKS ARE AT PRE-EXISTING ACTIVE CHROMATIN
---------------------------------------------------
- 84.4% of gained RUNX1 peaks colocalize with H3K27ac in BOTH conditions
- Only 8.6% of gained peaks lack H3K27ac entirely
- Gained peaks are more promoter-proximal (41.6% within 2kb of TSS vs 32.0% for maintained)
- Gained peaks carry higher ChIP signal (median fold-enrichment 6.85 vs 5.48 for maintained)

This pattern indicates that freed RUNX1 gains access to already-open, active regulatory elements that were previously occluded by the CBFβ-SMMHC oncoprotein complex.

KEY GENES GAINING RUNX1 BINDING
---------------------------------
RUNX1 gains de novo binding near critical hematopoietic regulators and oncogenes:

- MYC: 1 peak (56 bp from TSS) — master transcriptional amplifier
- CCND2: 4 peaks (at TSS) — cyclin D2, cell cycle regulation
- CEBPA: 1 peak (at TSS) — master myeloid differentiation factor
- GFI1: 3 peaks — transcriptional repressor, HSC maintenance
- EGR1: 2 peaks — immediate early gene, myeloid differentiation
- IRF1: 2 peaks — interferon regulatory factor
- TAL1: 1 peak (135 bp) — hematopoietic transcription factor
- LYL1: 4 peaks — hematopoietic transcription factor
- BCL2: 1 peak (at TSS) — anti-apoptotic protein
- JAK2: 1 peak (68 bp) — JAK-STAT kinase
- STAT5A: 1 peak (740 bp) — JAK-STAT signaling
- DEK: 1 peak (at TSS) — chromatin remodeling
- CD33: 1 peak (1,076 bp) — myeloid marker, therapeutic target
- SMAD7: 2 peaks — TGF-β pathway inhibitor
- FOS: 2 peaks — AP-1 component
- KLF6: 2 peaks — tumor suppressor

Notable: CEBPE (neutrophil differentiation factor) LOST RUNX1 binding, suggesting selective remodeling of the myeloid TF network.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
--------------------------
The CBFβ-SMMHC fusion oncoprotein (product of inv(16) translocation) forms aberrant complexes with RUNX1, sequestering it away from normal genomic targets (Lutterbach et al., 1999; Speck & Gilliland, 2007). This sequestration is a primary mechanism by which the fusion blocks myeloid differentiation.

AI-10-49 disrupts this aberrant interaction, liberating RUNX1 to engage chromatin. The resulting massive gain of binding at pre-existing active regulatory elements (84.4% H3K27ac-positive) demonstrates that:

1. Chromatin accessibility is NOT the limiting factor — RUNX1 binding sites exist but are occluded by the oncoprotein complex
2. The freed RUNX1 engages a normal differentiation program (CEBPA, GFI1, EGR1) that was suppressed by sequestration
3. RUNX1 redistribution is an EARLY event that precedes and is independent of H3K27ac changes (only 1.2% of gained H3K27ac peaks overlap RUNX1)

THERAPEUTIC IMPLICATIONS
--------------------------
- RUNX1 liberation may restore the myeloid differentiation program blocked by CBFβ-SMMHC
- Gained RUNX1 binding at MYC, CCND2, and JAK-STAT components suggests modulation of proliferation signaling
- RUNX1 binding at CD33 creates potential for combinatorial targeting with antibody-drug conjugates
- The retention of 92.7% of existing sites with massive gain of new sites suggests a permissive rather than repressive mechanism of therapeutic action

LIMITATIONS
------------
- Single replicate per condition (no formal statistical testing)
- Pre-called peaks only (no BAM-based count analysis)
- No motif enrichment or TF footprint analysis
- Biological interpretations are correlational, requiring experimental validation

REFERENCES
-----------
- Lutterbach B et al. (1999) Blood 93:3327-3337. PMID: 10216100
- Speck NA & Gilliland DG (2007) Nat Rev Cancer 7:345-358. PMID: 17446860
- Illendula A et al. (2015) Blood 126:2589. PMID: 26363797
- Illendula A et al. (2018) Sci Transl Med 7:314ra184. PMID: 26537258

**Task complete.** The `bulk_epigenomics_analyst` specialist was selected because its `When to use` literally matches: ChIP-seq peak BED/narrowPeak files needing differential peak analysis between conditions.

**Summary of results:**

RUNX1 chromatin occupancy increases ~6.9-fold upon CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition with AI-10-49:

| Metric | DMSO | AI-10-49 | Change |
|--------|------|----------|--------|
| RUNX1 peaks | 1,329 | 9,169 | +6.9x |
| Genomic coverage | 0.33 Mb | 3.18 Mb | +9.7x |
| H3K27ac peaks | 57,828 | 56,299 | Stable |

Of the 1,329 DMSO RUNX1 peaks, 1,232 (92.7%) are maintained, 97 (7.3%) are lost, and 7,950 new peaks are gained. Gained peaks colocalize with H3K27ac at 84.4% and are enriched at promoters (41.6% within 2 kb TSS) of key hematopoietic regulators including MYC, CEBPA, CCND2, GFI1, EGR1, and BCL2. The data support a model where CBFβ-SMMHC sequesters RUNX1, and AI-10-49 frees it to engage pre-existing active chromatin.
